Outcome: Prevalence of TM/herbal use for children (134 studies, 81,709 participants)
Study design and starting level: Cross-sectional and record-based prevalence studies (start high for a prevalence question)
Risk of bias: Not serious: pooled estimate unchanged when high-risk studies excluded (20.9%) or low-risk only (21.6%); subgroup by RoB P=0.34
Inconsistency: Serious: I2 99%, prediction interval 0.6% to 90.5%; only condition explains part of it
Indirectness: Serious: definitions of use differ (any TM, herbal only, healer only, spiritual; ever vs episode); several facility samples
Imprecision: Not serious: precise pooled CI (15% to 25%)
Publication bias: Undetected for inference; funnel asymmetry shown descriptively
Comment: About 1 in 5 caregivers used TM for their child; true value in a new setting may range widely

Imprecision: Serious for small groups (ARI k=5, convulsion k=7)
Comment: Higher in chronic conditions and general illness (35% to 39%) than diarrhoea and ARI (8%)

Study design and starting level: Mostly cross-sectional, few adjusted (24 of 143 associations)
Inconsistency: Not serious for education and SES (consistent direction)
Comment: Lower education (15 of 16 with clear direction) and lower SES (8 of 9) linked to higher use
